newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Products Outlook - Gas oil well supported.
newsitem.headline: Asia Products Outlook - Gas oil well supported.

text.p: Gas oil prices are expected to be well supported this week after a record 1.9 million barrels of diesel for end April/early May lifting exchanged hands in the Singapore spot market last Friday, traders said.
Two related Singapore oil trading firms and a Japanese trader were involved in purchasing the 12 cargoes on Friday, they said.
The prices ranged between $26.95 and $27.20 per barrel for end April cargoes, free-on-board (fob) basis, while early May cargoes traded between $26.70 and $26.80.
The local traders have to date bought at least a staggering 13 million barrels since March 3, helping to boost regional diesel prices and support refining margins.
"People are still expecting the market to go down, but these two buyers are holding it up," one trader said.
The Singapore trader might have already booked most available storage tank space in China for its massive diesel purchases, traders said.

The diesel market was given added support on news that a 27,500-barrel-per-day (bpd) hydrocracker at Indonesia's Dumai refinery was shut following a fire at the refinery late on Friday, and was expected to restart in late April.
Naphtha extended its losses on bearish sentiment amid ample prompt supplies, and was expected to remain in contango in the near-term.
Arbitrage supplies from the Mediterranean arriving in April-May added to the length and traders estimated over 300,000 tonnes still available for second-half May and early June.
Poor regional demand for gasoline beared down on prices and prompted a sharp build in Singapore stocks.
Light distillate stocks in Singapore for the week ending April 9 rose to a near two-year high at 7.237 million barrels, up 855,000 barrels from the previous week.
Traders said there were not many buyers despite the upcoming summer driving season in the northern hemisphere.
"The only demand is in Japan, but even they are not buying much," one seller said.
Scheduled refinery maintenance in Australia is expected to raise around two million barrels worth of demand in May and June, although serious buyers have yet to emerge, traders said.
The market is also looking to Taiwan for incremental demand in the hope that the next tender for cargoes to be delivered during second half May might soak up more of the surplus.
In the fuel oil market, most traders were uncertain about market direction, searching for fresh factors to stimulate the sluggish sentiment.
Routine cargoes from the Middle East are expected to continue to arrive in Singapore but the number will be slightly fewer than usual, which could support prices, traders said.
"But I think prices will just move narrowly without too much excitement," said one trader.

The low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) market was dampened further after Indonesia's state-owned Pertamina allocated an additional 700,000 barrels of LSWR to its affiliates for April loading, bringing the total to 4.3 million barrels, traders said.
Some 400,000-to-500,000 barrels scheduled for March lifting have also been rolled over for lifting in April, traders said.
There was also about one million barrels of straight-run LSWR available from Singapore and Malaysia in April, they said.
As a result, prices have slumped to less than $15.50 per barrel from a high of $16.25 early last week, traders said.
As regional requirements are at a seasonal low and demand in Japan is not expected to pick up for the summer in June, traders expected LSWR prices to fall below $15.00 per barrel soon.
Japanese traders also said they did not expect enquiries for LSWR from Japan to emerge until June.
